title: Feasibility, Usability and Preliminary Efficacy of Home-based FES Fro Adhesive Capsulitis
official: Feasibility, Usability and Preliminary Efficacy of Home-based FES Fro Adhesive Capsulitis
summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the feasibility, usability and preliminary efficacy of a home-based Functional Electrical Stimulation(FES) in individuals with shoulder adhesive capsulitis. The main question it aims to answer is if combining home-based FES to usual therapy at the clinic will improve pain and improve function of the impaired shoulder.

interventions.name: Home based FES in combination with usual therapy

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age \> 18 years
2. Individuals diagnosed with shoulder adhesive capsulitis
3. Shoulder pain, limited shoulder mobility for more than 4 weeks, normal shoulder x-ray findings, and normal neurological exam
4. Can tolerate electrical stimulation

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Presence of shoulder tumors or bone lesions
2. History of shoulder fracture or subluxation
3. History of shoulder surgery
4. Severe osteoporosis,
5. Rheumatic disease
6. Radiating pain from cervical radiculopathy
7. Participation in other clinical trial, and/or intraarticular steroid injections within 6 weeks
